title: The Pen(cil) Is Mightier Than the Laptop
author: Emily Cherkin
summary: Cherkin argues that EdTech has fundamentally harmed childhood by wrapping Big Tech's extractive model in an 'education' veneer. Schools now operate on 1:1 devices and AI tutors, fueling four crises: mental health collapse (screen use before age two linked to anxiety by 13), plummeting test scores, destroyed creativity, and democratic decay as children consume algorithm-driven content. The author rejects myths about digital literacy and offers four concrete acts: pause EdTech investment, audit platforms against effectiveness/safety/legality, implement AI moratoriums, and start tech-intentional community conversations. Best preparation for a digital future is an analog childhood.
points: Children 8-18 average 7.5 hours daily on screens; 62% of children under two watch YouTube.
Reading and math scores plummeted as EdTech rolled out; device-heavy schools have worst test scores.
EdTech kills creativity: if children cannot imagine flying, they cannot innovate.
The business model of EdTech is fundamentally at odds with healthy child development.
Schools must ask four questions before deploying any tech: effective? safe? legal? better than human?
